decisions.rationale: Verified by reading the test at 80eff5af (the reviewed bytes, hash matches): the strict while-running comparison and the identity check are applied only to the gear checklist and the two tags, and an element around the checklist is caught only by the rendered-width comparison, which reads one instant. An endless scale pulse on such an element that is at its identity value when read therefore passes. The pass counts (9 of 10 and 10 of 10) and the drawn-width samples are reported by the critic and were not re-run here; they are consistent with the code. The page breaks README task 11 Outcome, which forbids layout-affecting motion around the tags, and the behaviour predates loop 7. Under the owner's option A decision, an animation the test reads at one instant is a documented residual, so the defect to fix is that neither the lab.json residual sentence nor the solved-run record's not-covered list names animations on elements around the checklist. Smallest correct fix: name endless animations on elements around the gear checklist, and the run-to-run variation they can cause, in the lab.json residual sentence and in the next solved-run record's not-covered list, with no test change. Scope: inside the approved minimal loop-6 scope, as wording only. The critic's lead recommendation, a strict running-animation check on every ancestor up to the root, would be new detection reaching beyond the checklist and the tags. It would expand the contract and run against option A, so it is not adopted.

Verified on the 80eff5af lab.json bytes (hash matches) against 89161df6 and the 4cc61c8e record. Loop 7 added an 'endless one that changes a width or padding' clause to the residual example, and the record's not-covered list now limits every listed timing to width or padding animations. Read with the preceding sentence, which says the test rejects non-identity transform-type and zoom values, both texts suggest that a held scale or zoom is always caught. It is not. The test finishes every finite animation on the checklist and the tags whatever its play state, so a paused, very long or long-delayed finite animation is measured at its end values, and one that ends at identity passes. That is the owner-accepted cl5 residual, now understated. On 'paused', the code supports qualifying the word rather than dropping it. A paused finite animation ending at identity passes, while a paused endless one meets the strict branch and fails, as do finite ones whose held end is not identity. The learner-facing README line 17 and task 11 Outcome stay general and correct, so the impact is on maintainers and evidence readers, and low fits. Smallest correct fix: in one rewording of the lab.json residual sentence and the next record's not-covered list, describe the residual by timing and property: finite animations that the test jumps to an identity end value, of any size, padding, transform-type or zoom property, including paused, very long or long-delayed ones. Write it together with the cl7-edu-001 and cl7-sme-001 wording. Scope: inside the approved minimal loop-6 scope, wording only, with no behaviour change.

Verified on the current record (hash matches the reviewed bytes) and the 80eff5af test. The not-covered list narrowed from the 4cc61c8e wording, which named no property, to width or padding animations only, and lab.json narrowed the same way (see cl7-edu-002). Case 1, the owner-accepted cl5 residuals that finish at identity, follows directly from the finish-then-identity logic. Case 2 follows from the strict branch, which accepts the literal none keyword at the instant read, so endless keyframes that rest at none for part of each cycle can pass. Case 4 is the cl7-edu-001 ancestor case. Case 3, an endless zoom pulse on the checklist, rests on the critic's runs: code reading shows that zoom has no none keyword and that the checklist's zoom is read once before it is pinned, but whether it reads exactly one depends on the keyframes, so the reconciler attributes that result to the critic. It does not change the decision. Every case is either a finite animation jumped to its end or one read at a single instant, which is exactly what the owner's option A makes a documented residual, so none justifies a test change. The critic also asks for no new mechanism. Medium is fair, because these are wrong pages that pass in every reported run while no residual text names them, though the README forbids all four in general terms. Smallest correct fix: replace the record's not-covered list and the lab.json residual sentence with one consistent value-safe statement. It should name finite animations of any size, padding, transform-type or zoom property that end at identity, including qualified paused, very long or long-delayed ones. It should also name endless width, padding or zoom animations, endless transform-type animations whose value at the instant read is none or identity, animations on elements around the checklist, and animated custom properties. Optionally, list the none-resting, checklist zoom and surrounding-element pulses as known undetected variants. Scope: inside the approved minimal loop-6 scope and consistent with option A, wording only, with no test change.
